title: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
content: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus is transmitted by whiteflies. Infected tomato plants can become stunted and develop upward-curled leaves with yellowing; disease can reduce fruit set and yield when plants are infected early. North Carolina State Extension recommends planting resistant varieties where available, using virus-free transplants, excluding whiteflies from production areas when practical, managing whiteflies, and removing infected plants and weed hosts that can support the virus or vector.
author: Erik Murray, Barbara Reeves, Inga Meadows, Ella Hinchliffe, and Sara Villani
